**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] User mentioned Knicks Go is a retired Thoroughbred racehorse foaled on January 29, 2016.
- [FACT] Knicks Go was the 2021 American Horse of the Year after winning five of seven starts.
- [FACT] User stated Knicks Go won the Breeders' Cup Classic, Whitney Stakes, and Pegasus World Cup.
- [FACT] User noted Knicks Go won the Breeders' Cup Dirt Mile the year before.
- [FACT] User indicated Knicks Go is the sixth horse to win two different Breeders' Cup races.
- [FACT] User mentioned Knicks Go's other wins include the Breeders' Futurity as a two-year-old in 2018.
- [FACT] User stated Knicks Go finished second in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile.
- [FACT] User noted Knicks Go finished second in the 2022 Pegasus World Cup.
- [FACT] User indicated Knicks Go was retired to stud at Taylor Made Farm in Nicholasville, Kentucky.
- [FACT] User mentioned Knicks Go's initial stud fee was $30,000.
- [FACT] User described Knicks Go as a gray horse.
- [FACT] User stated Knicks Go was bred by Angie Moore and her daughter Sabrina at GreenMount Farm in Reisterstown, Maryland.
- [FACT] User noted Knicks Go is from the second crop of Paynter.
- [FACT] User mentioned Paynter won the Haskell Invitational and received social media attention for his battle against colitis and laminitis.
- [FACT] User stated Knicks Go was produced by Kosmo's Buddy, a stakes-winning daughter of Outflanker.
- [FACT] User indicated Kosmo's Buddy was claimed by the Moores for $40,000 near the end of a 37-race career.
- [FACT] User noted Knicks Go was sold as a weanling for $40,000 at the 2016 Keeneland November sale.
- [FACT] User stated Knicks Go was resold as a yearling at the Keeneland September 2017 sale for $87,000 to the Korea Racing Authority.
- [FACT] User mentioned Knicks Go was originally trained by Ben Colebrook and transferred to Brad Cox's stable at the end of 2019.
- [FACT] User explained the name Knicks Go is derived from the K-nicks breeding system used by the Korea Racing Authority (KRA).
- [FACT] User quoted Jun Park, a racing manager of the KRA, regarding the name Knicks Go.
